title: Short Stuff: Mullets: 'Nuff Said
summary: Short Stuff episode on the mullet hairstyle, short in front and long in back. Josh and Chuck trade personal haircut stories, then cover the origin of the term "mullet" (Beastie Boys' "Mullet Head," the mullet fish, the older "mullet head" insult, and a Mark Twain attribution the hosts call inaccurate). They trace the hairstyle back to ancient Greece (Homer's Iliad, Abantes spearmen) and prehistoric hunter-gatherers, then list famous mullet wearers (Andre Agassi, Billy Ray Cyrus, Paul and Linda McCartney, David Bowie, Jane Fonda, Florence Henderson, President James K. Polk) and movie examples. The episode closes with brief movie chat and the sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the short episode by joking about its length and then discuss their personal experiences with mullets, including a Tony Hawk-style skater cut and a yearbook photo.

segments.title: Mullet history and the Beastie Boys
segments.summary: The hosts say the term mullet is often credited to the Beastie Boys' song Mullet Head, and note that mullet head was an older insult for a dummy. They relay an explanation that the mullet fish rots from the neck down, which resembles the haircut.

segments.title: Mark Twain attribution and ancient mullets
segments.summary: The hosts say Mark Twain is often wrongly cited as coining the term mullet. They describe ancient examples, including Homer's Iliad and the Abantes spearmen with cropped forelocks and long backs, and prehistoric hunter-gatherers who may have trimmed hair for practical reasons.

segments.title: Famous mullet wearers
segments.summary: The hosts list famous mullet wearers, including Andre Agassi, a University of Florida center, Sean William Scott in Old School, Billy Ray Cyrus, and Will Ferrell's character in Old School's birthday party scene. They also mention Step Brothers and Role Models.

segments.title: Rock stars and other mullet examples
segments.summary: The hosts discuss David Bowie's Ziggy Stardust look as a debated mullet, the Paul and Linda McCartney matching mullets from the seventies, and the feemullet on Jane Fonda and Florence Henderson.

segments.title: President Polk and movie tangents
segments.summary: The hosts mention President James K. Polk as a mullet wearer, then bring up Last of the Mohicans and briefly discuss Murder on the Orient Express and an unnamed movie.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh closes the episode and credits the show's production company.
